Citizen

18 models on WRotate · 49 members own one

Citizen is a Japanese watch manufacturer known for its innovative technology, most notably its light-powered Eco-Drive watches. The company is one of the largest watch and movement manufacturers in the world, producing a wide range of timepieces from affordable quartz models to high-end mechanical and satellite-synchronized watches.

The story

The company's origins trace back to the Shokosha Watch Research Institute, founded in 1918 by Kamekichi Yamazaki. In 1924, they produced their first pocket watch, which was named "CITIZEN" by the then-mayor of Tokyo, Count Shinpei Goto, with the hope that it would become a timepiece cherished by all citizens. This name was adopted when the Citizen Watch Co., Ltd. was officially established in 1930, and the company released its first wristwatch in 1931. The post-war era saw significant innovation, including Japan's first calendar watch in 1952, the shock-resistant "Parashock" in 1956, and the country's first water-resistant watch, the "Parawater," in 1959. A notable early mechanical model was the "Junior," introduced in 1958 and aimed at the youth market. In the 1970s, Citizen experimented with new case materials and coatings, leading to models nicknamed "Blackie" for their novel black finish. A major turning point for Citizen was the pioneering of light-powered technology. In 1976, the company introduced the world's first analog quartz watch powered by a solar cell, the Crystron Solar Cell. This innovation evolved into the renowned Eco-Drive technology, officially launched in 1995, which can generate power from any light source and has become a cornerstone of the brand, featured in lines like the classic "Corso" and the military-inspired "Chandler" field watch. Another significant development was the introduction of the "Promaster" line in 1989, a series of professional-grade sports watches for use on land, at sea, and in the air. This line includes the popular "Promaster Diver" and the rugged "Promaster Tough" models. Today, Citizen continues to be a global leader in watchmaking, offering a diverse range of timepieces including sophisticated "Chronograph" models, modern sports designs like the "Odyn," and advanced "World Time Chronograph Alarm" watches, while also producing traditional "Mechanical" timepieces.
